In terms of the RMSE (Fig. 4 (b)), the TC (GSCD_TC) scheme performs better than other single-variable (multi-variable) calibration schemes. It's worth noting that the averaged RMSE for the GLEAM scheme is greater than that of the PML scheme, which is inconsistent with the results of the CC metric or streaflow simulation. This suggests that no single ET dataset consistently outperforms others in parameter calibration when evaluated with different variables or metrics. Moreover, the merged ET data may help reduce the uncertainty associated with raw ET data in large-scale parameter calibration. However, the Regression scheme demonstrates superior performance compared to other schemes in soil moisture simulation. This may be attributed to the inclusion of soil properties, which significantly affect VIC soil moisture simulation, in the regression relation-based parameter regionalization method proposed by Wu et al. (2007) . Evaluating the applicability of ET datasets for parameter calibration is widely recognized as a robust approach to evaluating gridded ET products (Dembele et al., 2020a; Guo et al., 2022 ), which is also demonstrated in this study by the consistency between the performance of the ET products assessed using the TC method (water balance method) (Fig. S1 ) and the parameter calibration method. During calibration, each parameter has its own reasonable feasible range. For example, the range of the parameter infilt was set from 0.0 to 0.40 (Fig. S3 ). This ensures that parameters do not vary significantly within the feasible range, even though different ET datasets vary in absolute values used for parameter calibration. This means that the uncertainties in parameter calibration caused by errors in ET products are controlled within a certain range (Guo et al., 2022 ). Our results highlight the superiority of the TC (GSCD_TC) scheme compared to other ET-based single-variable (multi-variable) calibration schemes in simulating streamflow and soil moisture. Possible reasons behined this may arise from the improved accuracy of the merged ET data based on the TC technique compared to the original ET datasets, as demonstrated in Fig. S1  and corroborated by some prior studies (Li et al., 2023b; Park et al., 2023 ). In terms of streamflow simulation, the GSCD scheme outperforms the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. However, the multi-variable calibration schemes do not consistently outperform the GSCD scheme. This observation can be attributed to the fact that the most influential variable for streamflow simulation in parameter calibration is streamflow itself. The introduction of a new variable as an additional objective may possibly reduce the streamflow simulation performance (Dembele et al., 2020b ). Given the critical dependence between ET and soil moisture, the improved representativeness of ET enhances the simulations of soil moisture (Mei et al., 2023 ). This helps explain why the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes yield better results in soil moisture simulation compared to the GSCD scheme.  4.2 Merged ET-based calibration scheme versus raw ET-based calibration schemes Since the differences in the performance of various schemes in soil moisture simulation are minimal, the subsequent presentation will primarily concentrate on the results of streamflow simulation. To assess whether the merged ET-based calibration scheme improved the performance of streamflow simulation, we conducted a comparison of the variation in NSE/KGE values between the TC scheme and three raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. As shown in Fig. 5  , the TC scheme exhibited the highest model performance in both daily (Fig. 5 (a)–(c)) and monthly (Fig. 5 (d)–(f)) streamflow simulations when compared to the three raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. The ranges of improvement in NSE and KGE for the simulated streamflow are 0.023 to 0.080 and 0.026 to 0.061, respectively. The enhanced applicability of the merged ET data in parameter calibration compared to the original ET datasets can be attributed to the improved accuracy of the merged ET data based on the TC method, as demonstrated using the water balance method (Fig. S1 ). These improvements are significant when compared to similar studies (Liu et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2022 ). For example, Liu et al. (2022)  reported that the calibration scheme using adjusted ET data based on the Choudhury-Budyko formula did not show any improvement compared to using raw RS ET data in monthly streamflow simulations. This finding suggests that the integration of ET data from various sources through merging techniques is an effective approach to enhancing the reliability of ET-based parameter calibration in ungauged catchments. However, it is important to note that although the merged ET-based calibration scheme has improved the overall accuracy of simulated streamflow in all 49 selected catchments compared to the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes, it may not necessarily improve the accuracy of streamflow simulations in the individual catchment. Specifically, there is a significant negative relationship between the variation of NSE/KGE values in the merged ET-based calibration scheme relative to that in the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes and the NSE/KGE values in the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. This indicates that in catchments where the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes exhibit poor performance, the merged ET-based calibration scheme offers a promising solution to improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation. Furthermore, we compared the differences in streamflow simulation performance between three raw RS ET-based multi-variable calibration schemes (GSCD_EBET, GSCD_GLEAM, and GSCD_PML schemes) and the GSCD_TC scheme (Fig. 6  ). The introduction of merged ET data in the multi-variable calibration scheme resulted in an improvement in the performance of streamflow simulation compared to the schemes that used both raw RS ET and GSCD data as calibration targets. However, this improvement is not found to be significant. This finding contrasts with the results observed in single-variable calibration schemes (Fig. 5 ), where the merged ET-based calibration scheme demonstrated a significant improvement in the performance of streamflow simulation. One potential explanation for this discrepancy could be that in the multi-variable calibration schemes, the calibration process aims to strike a balance between multiple objectives (GSCD and ET), instead of solely prioritizing the accuracy of ET data. Consequently, the sensitivity of the calibration process to the accuracy of ET data may be diminished. This could result in a smaller improvement in streamflow simulation performance compared to single-variable calibration schemes that exclusively optimize the accuracy of simulated ET. However, despite the overall insignificant improvement, the GSCD_TC scheme has demonstrated effectiveness in enhancing the accuracy of streamflow simulation in catchments where the GSCD_EBET, GSCD_GLEAM, and GSCD_PML schemes exhibited poor performance (i.e., catchments with NSE/KGE values for simulated daily streamflow not exceeding 0.50 or catchments with NSE/KGE values for simulated monthly streamflow not exceeding 0.60).  4.3 Multi-variable calibration schemes versus single-variable calibration schemes We conducted additional tests to evaluate whether the multi-variable calibration schemes exhibit superior performance in streamflow simulation compared to the single-variable calibration schemes. All the multi-variable calibration schemes demonstrate superior performance in streamflow simulation, both at the daily (Fig. 7  (a)−(d)) and monthly (Fig. 7 (e)−(h)) scales, compared to their corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. Among the four pairs of multi-variable calibration schemes and ET-based single-variable calibration schemes, the GSCD_EBET scheme exhibits the most significant improvement in streamflow simulation performance when compared to its corresponding EBET scheme. The average NSE (KGE) values for the daily (Fig. 7 (a)) and monthly (Fig. 7 (e)) simulated streamflow in the 49 selected catchments increased by 0.125 and 0.133 (0.114 and 0.122), respectively. In contrast, the improvements achieved by the GSCD_TC scheme in streamflow simulation performance compared to its corresponding TC scheme are relatively smaller compared to the other three pairs of schemes. The average NSE (KGE) values for the daily (Fig. 7 (d)) and monthly (Fig. 7 (h)) simulated streamflow in the 49 selected catchments increased by 0.060 and 0.054 (0.062 and 0.077), respectively. Moreover, there exists a significant negative relationship between the variations in NSE/KGE values observed in the four multi-variable calibration schemes in comparison to the corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes and the NSE/KGE values in the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. These findings indicate that, in catchments where ET-based single-variable calibration schemes exhibit poor performance, the multi-variable calibration schemes can significantly improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation compared to the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. However, in catchments where the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes already demonstrate satisfactory streamflow simulation performance, the potential benefits of adopting multi-variable calibration might not be significant or valuable. This might be attributed to the fact that the quality of GSCD data is not always highly reliable (Yang et al., 2019 ). The existence of uncertainty in GSCD data can introduce additional errors during the calibration process, consequently limiting the advantages that could be obtained from multi-variable calibration schemes. Furthermore, we compared the performance of the GSCD scheme with that of the multi-variable calibration schemes (Fig. 8  ). Compared to the GSCD scheme, the multi-variable calibration schemes have demonstrated overall improvements in streamflow simulation performance, as indicated by higher average NSE values across the selected 49 catchments. Among the four pairs of compared calibration schemes, the GSCD_TC scheme has shown the greatest improvement in streamflow simulation accuracy compared to the GSCD scheme. The average NSE values for the daily (Fig. 8 (d)) and monthly (Fig. 8 (h)) simulated streamflow increased by 0.028 and 0.026, respectively. However, it should be noted that this improvement is lower than the improvements observed between the multi-variable calibration schemes and the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes (Fig. 7 ). The comparable streamflow simulation performance of the GSCD_TC scheme and the GSCD scheme may be attributed to the fact that the parameters derived from both schemes exhibited similar spatial patterns (Fig. S3  and Table S2 ). Contrary to the results obtained for the NSE metric, in most cases (except for the monthly streamflow simulated by the GSCD_GLEAM and GSCD_TC schemes), the multi-variable calibration schemes have shown varying degrees of reduction in the average KGE values of the simulated streamflow compared to the GSCD scheme. The average reduction in KGE values ranges from −0.024 for the GSCD_PML scheme in simulated daily streamflow to −0.004 for the GSCD_TC scheme in simulated daily streamflow. This finding suggests that, compared to the GSCD scheme, the multi-variable calibration schemes may not necessarily provide better streamflow simulation results across all evaluation metrics. The effectiveness of these multi-variable calibration schemes might depend on the reliability of the additional variable introduced in the calibration process (i.e., ET in this study). The decline in streamflow simulation performance in a multi-variable calibration scheme compared to the streamflow-based single-variable calibration is also reported in previous studies (Dembele et al., 2020b; Zhang et al., 2021 ). Two reasons could contribute to the lower average KGE values observed in the multi-variable calibration schemes compared to the GSCD scheme. Firstly, incorporating multiple data sources (i.e., GSCD and ET in this study) may introduce inconsistencies, such as differences in data quality, which can affect the reliability of model parameter calibration and subsequently impact the accuracy of the streamflow simulation. Secondly, multi-variable calibration involves trade-offs between different objectives (Dile et al., 2020; Koppa et al., 2019 ). This trade-off may not always result in the best performance for all evaluation metrics, leading to lower performance on a specific indicator like KGE.  4.4 Impact of climate conditions on the relative performance of the proposed calibration schemes In this section, taking AI as an example, we investigated whether the improvement in simulated streamflow varies under different climate conditions when comparing the merged ET-based calibration scheme (multi-variable calibration schemes) with the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes (ET-based single-variable calibration schemes). In Fig. 9  , the variation of NSE/KGE values in the TC scheme relative to that in the raw RS ET-based calibration scheme is depicted alongside the AI values. The results indicate that when comparing the TC scheme with the EBET scheme or the PML scheme, the improvements in the accuracy of simulated streamflow are substantially higher in arid regions than in humid regions. This disparity is particularly pronounced when evaluating the accuracy of monthly streamflow simulations. For example, the average variation of NSE (KGE) between the TC scheme and the PML scheme for daily streamflow in arid regions is 0.109 (0.167), whereas it is only 0.014 (0.008) in humid regions. However, there is an exception in the variation of the NSE metric for daily streamflow between the TC scheme and the EBET scheme, where the average variation of NSE in humid regions (0.074) is slightly higher than that in arid regions (0.058). Moreover, the improvements in simulated streamflow in arid regions are relatively small and similar to those in humid regions on average when comparing the TC scheme with the GLEAM scheme. We further examined the relationship between the variation of NSE/KGE values in the four multi-variable calibration schemes relative to the corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes and AI values. As shown in Fig. 10  , the multi-variable calibration schemes demonstrate improved performance in simulated streamflow in both arid and humid regions compared to their corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. These results indicate that incorporating streamflow characteristics into the calibration process based on ET data can improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation under various climatic conditions. However, the improvements in streamflow simulation accuracy are much more significant in arid regions compared to humid regions, especially when quantized using the KGE metric. For example, when comparing the GSCD_EBET scheme to the EBET scheme in terms of simulating daily streamflow, the average increase in NSE (KGE) is 0.178 (0.270) in arid regions, whereas it is 0.107 (0.059) in the humid regions. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the merged ET-based calibration scheme and multi-variable calibration schemes in enhancing the reliability of streamflow simulation, particularly in arid regions compared to humid regions. The significant improvements in streamflow simulation in arid regions have important implications for extending our research to other arid regions without the need for extensive validation using in-situ observations. The observed outcomes can potentially be attributed to the following factors: the three RS ET-based calibration schemes demonstrate comparatively superior performance in humid regions when compared to arid regions (Fig. 3 ). Furthermore, in arid regions, ET constitutes a larger portion of the total precipitation. Consequently, even minor inaccuracies in ET simulations can have a substantial impact and result in magnified errors in streamflow simulations (Liu et al., 2022 ). Therefore, improving the accuracy of ET estimation through the TC-based merging method or incorporating streamflow characteristics during the calibration process based on the ET data can help mitigate the influence of uncertainty in raw RS-based ET estimates on parameter calibration. As a result, the improvements in streamflow simulation in humid regions may not be as significant as those in arid regions.   5 Discussion 5.1 Uncertainties in ET-based calibration schemes Calibrating hydrological models in ungauged catchments remains a significant challenge. The emergence of RS-based ET products with improved spatiotemporal resolution and extensive spatial coverage has provided a promising solution for parameter calibration in such catchments (Dembele et al., 2020b; Liu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2021 ). The improved spatiotemporal resolution allows for individual parameter calibration within each grid using ET data (Fig. S3 ). This has the potential to decrease the uncertainty linked to lumped calibration solely relying on observed streamflow (Huang et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2022 ). Furthermore, the calibration of parameters using ET data can effectively circumvent the time-consuming computational process required for routing spatially distributed runoff, which offers significant advantages when compared to the parameter calibration approach based on observed streamflow (Jiang et al., 2020 ). However, it is crucial to acknowledge that the accuracy of ET data and uncertainties in ET simulation within hydrological modeling are two crucial factors influencing the performance of using ET data for parameter calibration (Liu et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2020 ). The fundamental principle underlying ET-based parameter calibration asserts that the accuracy of ET significantly impacts the reliability of parameter calibration, subsequently influencing the accuracy of streamflow and soil moisture simulation (Jiang et al., 2020; Kunnath-Poovakka et al., 2016 ). The merged ET-based calibration scheme exhibited improved performance in streamflow and soil moisture simulation when compared to the three raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. This improvement suggests that the merging method based on TC technology can effectively mitigate the uncertainty associated with the raw RS ET products, as demonstrated in prior studies (Li et al., 2023b; Park et al., 2023 ) and illustrated in Fig. S1 , thereby providing better constraints for hydrological parameters calibration. Generally, there are three assumptions for the TC technology: (i) All three datasets within a triple have a linear relationship with the true value; (ii) The errors associated with each dataset are independent; (iii) The errors from each dataset are uncorrelated with the true value (Li et al., 2023a; Li et al., 2023b; Park et al., 2023 ). However, numerous studies have demonstrated that some of these assumptions are frequently violated in practice applications, particularly for assumption (ii) (Dong et al., 2020; Jia et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023a ). In this study, both GLEAM and EBET data utilize the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Reanalysis product as input, which may violate assumption (ii) to some extent and increase the possibility of error cross-correlation. Recently, Li et al. (2022)  examined the uncertainty of five global ET products using multiple collocation algorithms. The results of their study suggested that the influence of nonzero error cross-correlation was acceptable, despite the inclusion of ECMWF meteorological reanalysis data in some of the evaluated ET products. Therefore, the influence of nonzero error cross-correlation on our findings is no longer directly examined or discussed here. Instead, the emphasis is redirected toward providing additional evidence to support the effectiveness of the merged ET based on the TC technology in parameter calibration. This is achieved by conducting a comparison between the TC scheme and EW scheme. As illustrated in Fig. 11  , the TC scheme demonstrated superior performance in simulating both daily and monthly streamflow compared to the EW scheme, as evaluated by the NSE/KGE metrics. It is worth noting that the EW scheme exhibited slightly better performance than three raw RS ET-based calibrated schemes (Table 2 ) in terms of simulated daily streamflow. Furthermore, the EW scheme also outperformed both the EBET scheme and PML scheme in terms of simulated monthly streamflow. These findings highlight the significant contribution of merged ET data in mitigating the uncertainty associated with raw RS-based ET data on parameter calibration. Particularly, when a proper merging approach is employed, the reduction in uncertainty becomes even more significant. Furthermore, the superior performance of streamflow simulation achieved by the TC scheme compared to the EW scheme also indicates that, despite the possibility of some assumptions of the TC technology being violated during the merging of three raw ET datasets, the TC-based merging method still offers broader application prospects in enhancing the reliability of RS-based ET products for parameter calibration in ungauged catchments. The merged ET based on the TC method inevitably incorporates the climatology of reference data. Therefore, the accuracy of the merged ET may also depend on the accuracy of the reference data used during the TC analysis (Yin and Park, 2021 ). To analyze the influence of the reference data on merged ET-based parameter calibration, we compared the performance of the TC_VIC scheme, which uses the VIC ET climatology from the Regression scheme as the reference during the ET merge, with that of the TC scheme. As shown in Fig. S4 , although the relative performance of the TC_VIC scheme compared to the TC scheme may vary across specific catchments, the TC_VIC scheme generally demonstrated comparable performance in simulating both daily and monthly streamflow to that of the TC scheme. The comparable streamflow simulation performance between the TC_VIC scheme and the TC scheme can be partially attributed to the similar climatologies between VIC ET from the Regression scheme and PML data (Fig. S5 ). Previous studies, such as those by Li et al. (2023b)  and Peng et al. (2021) , have highlighted the importance of the reference product's quality during the TC analysis for the accuracy of merged products. Furthermore, it's noted that a more accurate reference product typically results in higher precision merged results (Afshar et al., 2019 ). The consistency observed between the evaluation results using the TC method and those from the other two evaluation methods (Figs. 2  and S1 ) suggests that the TC method can be considered a validated approach for evaluating ET datasets. Consequently, in future studies, the selection of the reference climatology can be based on the evaluation results of the TC method to improve the reliability of the final merged results. It's crucial to highlight that the assessment was conducted using the VIC model. The deficiencies in the VIC model regarding ET simulation, such as its assumption that soil evaporation only occurs in unvegetated areas (Sun et al., 2021 ), may impact the performance of the compared parameter calibration schemes. Previous studies have demonstrated that calibrated parameters can compensate model structure problems (Bock et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2019 ). Even though our results demonstrated that the merged ET-based calibration scheme outperforms the three raw ET-based calibration schemes, it does not guarantee more physically realistic model parameters. This potential lack of physical realism in parameters calibrated using ET data can be seen as a necessary compromise to reduce the uncertainty in ET simulation associated with the model structure. This suggests that parameters obtained through calibration using reasonable ET data have the potential to compensate for deficiencies in the model structure, resulting in relatively satisfactory simulation results. Despite acknowledged deficiencies in the VIC model structure regarding ET simulation, all calibration schemes are implemented using the VIC model. Consequently, we hypothesize that the impact of model structure problems on different schemes may be comparable, suggesting that model structure problems might not significantly influence our conclusions. Exploring how model structure problems impact ET-based parameter calibration and subsequent simulation results is an inherently interesting and valuable research question. However, it appears that such an investigation is beyond the scope of this study, and problems related to the model structure are not challenges that can be addressed within this study. In the future, greater emphasis should be placed on reducing the deficiencies in hydrological models related to ET modeling. Once a hydrological model with enhanced reliability in ET simulation becomes available, it is anticipated to improve the performance of the merged ET-based parameter calibration scheme.  5.2 Which scheme is recommended to choose? The conventional practice of calibrating hydrological models solely against a single variable can frequently lead to parameter uncertainty. In such cases, considering a multi-variable calibration approach can serve as a potential solution to address this issue (Dembele et al., 2020a; Shah et al., 2021 ). Therefore, we conducted further examination to determine whether the multi-variable calibration schemes based on ET and streamflow characteristics improved the reliability of parameter estimation in ungauged catchments in comparison to the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. The results of our study indicated that the multi-variable calibration schemes significantly improved the accuracy of simulated streamflow in comparison to their corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. However, when compared to the GSCD scheme, the multi-variable calibration schemes demonstrated superior performance in terms of the NSE metric, while showing varying degrees of reduction in the average KGE values in most cases. Numerous previous studies have made efforts to evaluate whether multi-variable calibration schemes outperform single-variable calibration schemes, leading to conflicting and inconclusive outcomes (Dembele et al., 2020b; Huang et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022; Mei et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2021 ). For example, Liu et al. (2022)  discovered that multi-variable calibration schemes, which incorporated both ET and terrestrial water storage change as calibration targets, resulted in superior streamflow simulation accuracy compared to single-variable calibration schemes that relied solely on ET or terrestrial water storage change. In contrast, Mei et al. (2023)  reached a different conclusion. They found that the inclusion of an additional variable alongside runoff did not lead to an improvement in streamflow simulation. However, it did result in an improved simulation performance for the additional variable itself. The disagreements between these studies serve as a poignant reminder of the challenges and complexities that arise when attempting to simultaneously use multiple variables from various sources in parameter calibration. The reason behind this can be attributed to two key points: Firstly, the limitations associated with variables from various sources, such as differences in spatiotemporal resolutions and accuracy, lead to significant trade-offs in multi-variate calibration (Dile et al., 2020; Koppa et al., 2019 ). Secondly, the most influential variable for streamflow simulation in parameter calibration is streamflow-related variables (e.g., streamflow, runoff, and streamflow characteristics) (Dembele et al., 2020b; Mei et al., 2023 ). As a result, multi-variable calibration schemes that incorporate RS-based data and streamflow-related variables may not necessarily outperform single-variable calibration schemes based solely on streamflow-related variables. While the multi-variable calibration schemes exhibit only marginal improvements in streamflow simulation compared to the GSCD scheme, the GSCD_TC scheme should be considered the optimal choice in practical applications. This is because parameter calibration scheme solely based on GSCD or other streamflow characteristics datasets has certain limitations in practical applications. Firstly, hydrological models are continually advancing towards finer spatial resolutions. However, the resolution of streamflow characteristics imposes limitations on the calibrated parameter resolution. Calibrating at a higher resolution with this method may prove more challenging due to increased computational costs and potentially higher uncertainty in estimates of gridded streamflow characteristics (Yang et al., 2019 ). Secondly, in estimating streamflow characteristics using observed streamflow, Beck et al. (2015)  excluded watersheds influenced by human activities. However, streamflow characteristics have been significantly influenced by recent hydraulic infrastructures (Dal Molin et al., 2023 ). Therefore, in catchments with strong anthropogenic influences, the sole utilization of streamflow characteristics as a calibration target should be approached cautiously. Multi-variable calibration, incorporating both streamflow characteristics and ET data, has the potential to better constrain a hydrological model in such scenarios (Dembele et al., 2020a ).  5.3 Summary and further directions This study endeavors to provide solutions to the challenges encountered in parameter calibration for ungauged catchments. Compared to previous research, this study contains the following two novel elements: (i) This study conducts the first assessment to determine whether the calibration scheme, utilizing merged ET data based on the TC technology as the calibration target, improves the accuracy of streamflow simulation in ungauged catchments when compared to the calibration scheme that relies solely on raw RS-based ET data. (ii) The incorporation of both ET and streamflow characteristics as calibration targets is a novel multi-variable calibration approach introduced in this study. This approach enables the validation of whether the multi-variable calibration schemes help mitigate the impact of uncertainty in raw RS-based ET data on parameter calibration. Our findings demonstrate that both the proposed merged ET-based single-variable calibration scheme and the multi-variable calibration schemes, which utilize ET and streamflow characteristics as calibration targets, are significantly superior to the raw RS ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. This study opens up possibilities for utilizing globally available RS-based ET products to further improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation in ungauged catchments. Certainly, we acknowledge that this study is subject to several limitations. Firstly, the TC-based merging technology was innovatively adopted to improve the applicability of RS-based ET data in parameter calibration. However, it is worth considering that other RS-based datasets, such as soil moisture, could also provide valuable information for parameter calibration (Zhang et al., 2021 ). Future research efforts could explore whether the TC-based merging technology remains applicable and effective in enhancing the applicability of RS-based soil moisture data in parameter calibration. Secondly, we proposed a multi-variable calibration scheme by combining streamflow characteristics and ET data as calibration targets. Our findings demonstrated that this multi-variable calibration scheme exhibits higher reliability compared to the ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. In this study, only two streamflow characteristics, namely RC and BFI, were chosen from a variety of options. This selection potentially results in a loss of valuable information reflecting the streamflow time series (Yang et al., 2019 ). To improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation in ungauged catchments, it is recommended that future research endeavors explore the incorporation of a broader range of streamflow characteristics and other RS-based variables during the multi-variable calibration process. Thirdly, our results indicate that the improvements in streamflow simulation performance from the proposed calibration schemes are more pronounced in arid regions than in humid regions. However, there are more catchments in humid regions (approximately 73.5 % of the total catchments) due to easier access to observed streamflow data in those regions (Fig. 1  and Table S1 ). Despite this imbalance may introduce uncertainty into our results, the proposed calibration schemes offer viable solutions to improve the reliability of streamflow simulation in ungauged catchments, especially in arid regions.   6 Conclusions This study, motivated by the goal of enhancing the reliability of hydrological simulation in ungauged catchments, compared two methods designed to mitigate the impact of raw RS-based ET data uncertainty on parameter calibration. The first method leveraged merged ET data obtained from the TC technology for parameter calibration, while the second introduced multi-variable calibration schemes incorporating both ET and streamflow features (RC and BFI in this study) as calibration objectives. The VIC model was implemented across 49 catchments in China to evaluate the potential improvements offered by these two methods in hydrological simulation compared to three traditional raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. The key findings and conclusions are summarized as follows: (1) Both the merged ET-based calibration scheme and the multi-variable calibration schemes improved the reliability of streamflow simulation when compared to the raw RS ET-based calibration schemes. In most calibration schemes, streamflow simulation tends to be less accurate in relatively dry catchments compared to relatively humid catchments. (2) All the multi-variable calibration schemes demonstrated superior performance in streamflow simulation when compared to their corresponding ET-based single-variable calibration schemes. (3) Generally, the effectiveness of both the merged ET-based calibration scheme and multi-variable calibration schemes in enhancing the reliability of streamflow simulation is significantly higher in arid catchments compared to humid catchments. This finding has significant implications for expanding the research to other arid catchments without necessitating extensive validation via in-situ observations. In summary, both the merged ET-based single-variable calibration and multi-variable calibration schemes provide practical solutions for parameter estimation in ungauged catchments. These schemes have the potential to improve the reliability of streamflow simulations and offer valuable support for water resources management and decision-making in ungauged catchments. Future research could investigate the viability of the TC-based merging technology for improving the utility of other RS-based variables in parameter calibration. Additionally, it would be beneficial to examine the inclusion of a wider array of streamflow features, as well as other RS-based variables, in the multi-variable calibration process.
1 Introduction The joint influence of climate change and human activity is undeniably catalyzing a surge in extreme weather events in lots of regions, including an increase in heatwaves, floods, and droughts, which may damage the ecosphere and create profound negative impacts on societal well-being all together (Cianconi et al., 2015 ). As stated in the 2021 IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) Sixth Assessment Report, the proportion of floods among all disasters has increased from 40 % in 2007 to 61.66 % in 2021, and the floods will become more severe in the warmer future (Douville et al., 2021; Jonkman and Vrijling, 2008 ). The escalation of severe flooding events could be tied to the spatial and temporal distribution of water resources. In areas where water is plentiful, the frequency of floods appears to show the trend of rise which may be attributed to shifts in climate patterns (Tabari., 2020 ). The combination of floods in the mainstream and the tributaries may generally cause the large floods downstream (Prohaska and llic, 2010 ). Under this background, deeper analysis in hydrological changes and the correlation between the factors of flood between the mainstream and its tributaries, can not only provide a theoretical basis for the formulation of dispatching plans, but also offer a reference for the construction of flood control facilities in the downstream (Li et al., 2022 ). Flood events are typically characterized by two fundamental elements: the duration and the magnitude of the flood. A situation where multiple rivers occur flood at once is known as a flood coincident event which can lead to the exacerbated damage downstream due to the merging of their peak flows (Reddy and Ganguli, 2013). The traditional method of studying flood coincidence is by counting the flood coincidence events from the observed data series and calculating the corresponding probabilities (Guo et al., 2011 ). The drawback of this approach is that it only focuses on historical flood events and cannot calculate the probability of encountering floods with different return periods. What’s more, due to intricate interconnections in the spatial network of flood events, single-site and single-variable models fall short in capturing the complex interplay between a river and its tributaries (Chen et al., 2012 ). The copula function, a novel analytical tool for assessing the interdependence between variables, made its financial sector debut in 1999. It subsequently gained widespread acceptance within hydrological analysis. Its application has since burgeoned, becoming a focal point in scientific research addressing an array of extreme weather events. For example, they have been employed in the study of drought frequency analysis(Xu et al., 2015 ;Abdi et al.,2017 ;Meimandi et al., 2024 ), rainfall frequency analysis(Yu et al.,2023 ; Bezak et al., 2019; Nazeri Tahroudi et al., 2022 ), flood frequency analysis(Razmkhah et al., 2022 ;Li and Zheng, 2016 ; Klaho et al., 2022 ), sea storm analysis(Yang and Qian, 2019 ;Bushra et al., 2019 ; Rueda et al., 2016 ) and some other theoretical analysis on the extreme problems(Quan et al., 2017 ; Yanto et al., 2023). Exploring the intricate phenomenon of flood coincidence demands a focused analysis on multivariate hydrological dynamics, where the interconnected nature of flood variables particularly counts. It is in this multifaceted context that the copula model proves to be an outstanding tool, adept at elucidating the intricate dependencies among these variables, as Requena et al. (2016)  highlighted. Yan et al. (2010)  harnessed the capabilities of the copula model to forge an integrated analysis of flood peak occurrence time and magnitude by utilizing hydrological data from gauges along the Qing and Yangtze Rivers. Similarly, Peng et al. (2019)  employed the same statistical technique to clarify the complexities of flood frequency in the Jinsha and Min Rivers, casting light on the correlations among time, magnitude, and spatial dimensions. In recent years, the nonstationary hydrological study has attracted a great deal of attention because of the increasing attention paid to the climate change (Hui et al.,2018; Sun et al., 2020 ; Gao et al., 2016). Recently, various methodologies using a probabilistic model of flood frequency considering nonstationary has been introduced (Su and Chen, 2019; Sen et al.,2020; He et al.,2021 ). The time-varying moment approach has gained widespread usage for incorporating time-varying probabilistic parameters to emulate the evolving behavior of extreme hydrometeorological variables in univariate scenarios (Zhou et al.,2022; Pan et al., 2019; Pathiraja et al.,2018 ). The employment of non-stationary approaches in time series is necessary to model the trend in the time series. The non-stationary marginal distribution in a conditional multivariate model based on copula was first studied by Zhang (2005) . The dependence was assumed to be constant over time. Chebana et al. (2013)  were the first to propose the utilization of copula functions with time-varying parameters when the dependence structure between the variables under investigation changes. Several questions hindered the study of multivariate non-stationary statistics. Firstly, when the marginal distribution family varies over time, how can we issue? When constructing multivariate hydrological models, it's typically necessary to consider multiple hydrological models. Furthermore, it's not only about current values, but also about anticipating future potential trends. Secondly, the length of the time series often imposes the limitation on the study from the piratical point. Bender et al. (2014)  applied time windows to obtain the time-varying parameters to analyze their impacts on the trend of the joint probability of flood peak and volume in four cases: (1) considering all parameters as time dependent; (2) considering the location and scale parameter of the marginals and the copula parameter as time dependent; (3)considering the location parameter of the marginals and the copula parameter as time dependent, and (4) considering only the copula parameter as time dependent. Currently, the research on the flood coincidence is typically based on stationary condition(Wang et al.,2009 ; Bing et al., 2018). The assumption that the parameters of the marginal distribution as well as the dependence structure are stationary may cover up their impacts on the multivariate statistical analysis (Zeng et al., 2019 ). The similar critical aspects of non-stationary states in the flood coincidence have yet to become focal points of comprehensive study which indicate there are remaining avenues of research ripe for exploration. The focus of this paper revolves around calculating the joint probability of key hydrological variables including flood time and flood peak discharge in the context of Huai River and its tributaries, Hong River, and Shi River. Although there are huge risks of flood coincidence, very few studies are conducted to research it between Huai River and its tributaries. Feng et al. (2020)  adeptly utilized the copula approach to probe into the coincidence of flooding between the Hong River and the upstream of Huai River, pinpointing mid-July as the peak period of overlap. Although insightful, the study only focuses on temporal coincidence and overlooked the significance of flood peak flow and the nonstationary research. Here, we first use several sets of models to fit the daily flow data to obtain the marginal distribution. Then, time-varying copula function combined with the moving window are applied to gain the dynamitic CP of flood across Huai River mainstream and its tributaries. For one hand, with the help of analyzing the nonstationary changes of parameters of the joint and marginal distribution, we shall investigate the roles they play in the probability of encountering flood events during the monsoon season in different years. For another hand, the trend that how the CP change shall be analyzed by moving time windows. The study region and data will be described in Section 2 . The subsequent section, Section 3 , will introduce the concept of the copula methodologies, explore several marginal distribution models, engage in methodological testing discussions, and show the principles of sliding time windows. Then the results shall be displayed and discussed in the sub-sections of Section 4 . We will draw final conclusions in Section 5 .  2 Study area and dataset The Huai River is located between Yangtze River and Yellow River in the east of China. It has catchment area of 270 thousand km2  with a population of approximately 201 million. Its northern part belongs to the temperate monsoon climate zone, whereas the southern part belongs to the subtropical monsoon climate zone. The area under study is geographically positioned between 114°15′E-117°80′E and 31°20′N-35°45′N. The basin's mean annual precipitation is recorded at 883 mm, with temperatures ranging between 11°C and 16°C (Girma et al., 2023 ). The observed temperature in this basin has increased since 1959 with the speed of 0.228℃ per year (Yang et al., 2012). Rainfall is mostly concentrated in the summer, accounting for 49 % of the annual total precipitation in the Huai River basin (Sun et al., 2019 ). The river's tributaries which are arranged in a fan-shaped catchment accelerate the convergence of floodwaters, thereby increasing the likelihood of flooding incidents. Historical records show that since 1950, the region has been hit by several devastating floods, including in the years 1954, 1991, 2003, 2007, and 2020, causing significant damage to densely populated areas. According to the research of Ma et al. (2014) , the change of climate and human activities have resulted in more flood days in one year in this region. The Shi River and Hong River, the tributaries of the Huai River, eventually merge with the main channel in Anhui Province. As same as Huai River, the flood CP of the Hong River and the Shi River is the highest from June to September. Therefore, the flood coincidence research is crucially important for a correct estimation of flood magnitude in the downstream area. To support our inquiry, we utilized daily discharge records spanning an extensive period of 58 years from January 1, 1959, to December 31, 2016, collected from three river gauging stations within the study area. The datasets for these gauges are notably complete, with no missing information. We extract the annual maximum series from the runoff series to conduct the research of flood peak. To address the question of the trend of the river's flow over time as well as the non-stationary variations of flood characteristics, our methodology is the use of 30-year sliding time windows. These windows were chosen for their validities because it is long enough to include a sufficient dataset for discerning dependency structures, yet short enough to maintain data reliability (with no discernible trends at the 95 % confidence level). The Wangjiaba gauge is situated along the Huai River, and Bantai and Jiangjiaji gauges are located on the Hong River and Shi River, respectively ( Fig. 1 ).  3 Methodology The structured methodology of the analysis is illustrated in  Fig. 2 . As depicted, the study's concept of coincidence encompasses the peak timing, peak flow magnitude of floods. To calculate the stationary probabilities for each characteristic, the process unfolds in three distinct steps: (1) extract the annual maximum daily average flow series as the peak flow series and the dates corresponding to the most severe flood as peak flow time series in each gauge; (2) estimate the parameters of marginal distributions; (3) find the fittest copula function that describes the co-occurrence of flood peak and flood timing in two pairs of gauging stations and calculate the CP. When considering non-stationary scenarios, the methodology includes additional steps. These involve applying the Mann-Kendall (MK) test to discern any trends across the data series from various rivers and divide the whole data into 29 sub-time series with the help of moving time windows. The subsequent phase of this study involves the application of time-varying parameters of marginal distributions and the copula function, aiming to derive diverse nonstationary coincidence probabilities related to timing and peak flow of floods. This process begins by determining both the probability associated with the timing of floods and the probability of encountering peak flows across various magnitudes between the gauging stations. Multiplying these probabilities yields the overall probability of nonstationary coincidence during the flood season. This can be used to analyze its trend and the difference from the stable encounter probability. 3.1 Copula function First conceptualized in 1959, the copula function is a groundbreaking mathematical tool that untangles the complexities of multivariate joint distributions. It achieves this by dissecting the joint distribution of 'n' random variables into their individual marginal distributions and one copula function. This method facilitates an intricate analysis by dissociating the inherent randomness of the variables from their interdependencies. Concretely, if we consider a joint distribution f ( x  1   , x  2   , x  3   , ⋯ , x  n   )    for the variables X  1   , X  2   , X  3   , ⋯ , X  n   ,    and their corresponding marginal distributions are denoted as F  1   x  1      , F  2   x  2      , F  3   x  3      , ⋯ , F  4   x  n        , respectively, then there exists a copula function C u  1   , u  2   , u  3   , … , u  n         that ensures the following relationship holds true:(1) f x  1   , x  2   , ⋯ , x  n      = C F  1   x  1      , F  2   x  2      , ⋯ , F  n   x  n         = C u  1   , u  2   , ⋯ , u  n          where F  i   x  i      = u  i      for i = 1 , 2 , ⋯ , n    with u  i   ∈ U ( 0 , 1 )   . Moving with the times, the study of copulas has embraced the temporal dimension. Time-dependent copulas have been designed to accommodate non-stationarity by allowing both the parameters of marginal distributions and copula function to fluctuate over a dynamic timeline. The interplay within bivariate copulas can be portrayed thusly:(3) F  X , Y   x , y    = C u , v θ  t         = C F  X   x α  t         , F  Y   y β  t         θ  t             where α  t    , β  t     and θ  t     denote the time-varying parameters of the marginal and joint distribution and can be estimated by Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). This study compares four typical Copulas—Clayton, Gumbel, Gaussian, and Frank—analyzing their bivariate formulations to deduce the most suitable one for joint distribution. The bivariate formula is displayed in Table S1.  3.2 Marginal distribution 3.2.1 VM-based distribution to model the peak timing of Huai Basin The circular statistical approaches are often employed in the studies of flood peak timing because of the cyclical nature of their timing (Lee et al., 2015 ). The VM distribution which was originally forged as a tool to measure atomic weight has branched out into a myriad of fields with remarkable utility (Benlakhdar et al., 2022). This model is one of the most fundamental models for describing the direction of the data well (Zhang et al.,2023 ). It can transform the date into the range of 0–2π by imposing constraints on the direction of the data. The transformation is defined by the equation:(4) x  i   = 2 π D  i    L        Here, D  i     signifies D   day of the i   year on which the maximum flood peaks, translating into the radian measurement x  i    , while L   encapsulates the flood season's full duration and for Huai River, L   equals 122. Diving deeper, the probability density function (PDF) of the univariate VM distribution can be expressed as:(5) f x  i   : κ , μ    = 1  2 π I  0   ( κ )   exp { κ cos (  x  i   − μ ) }     where κ   is the scale parameter, measuring the concentration of x  i    ; μ   is the location parameter, μ ∈ [ 0,2 π ]   . These parameters are estimated by MLE.  3.2.2 GEV-based distribution to model the peak flow in Huai Basin The GEV distribution has been widely employed in the flood risk analysis for its reliability in describing the extreme values (Van Dusen et al., 2020; Lima et al., 2016 ). The formulation of GEV distribution can be expressed as follows:(6) f x ; α , β , ξ    = 1  β   ( 1 + α x − ξ  β      )  − 1  α − 1     × e  − ( 1 + α x − ξ  β      )  − 1  α − 1           Where α stands as the shape parameter; β   emerges as the scale parameter, setting the distribution's breadth; ξ operates as the location parameter, anchoring the distribution's central position.   3.3 Tests of goodness-of-fit 3.3.1 The akaike information criterion and the bayesian information criterion Based on the concept of entropy, AIC is a criterion for measuring the goodness of fit of statistical models (Akaike,1998 ). The penalty term of BIC is larger than that of AIC, considering the sample size. When there is an excess of samples, it can effectively prevent excessive model complexity caused by overly high model accuracy. The goodness of lower AIC or BIC scores is in their suggestion of a better-fitting model. These measures reveal themselves mathematically as:(7) AIC = − 2 ln L  ˆ     + 2 × k     (8) BIC = − 2 ln L  ˆ     + k × ln ( n )     where L  ˆ    is the peak likelihood, the model achieves;k   represents the count of parameters in the model; n stands for the number of data points sampled.  3.3.2 The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test Moving to the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, it's an effective, nonparametric method used to assess the probability distribution of a sample series. It has two versions: the One-Sample KS test, comparing a sample series to a known distribution, and the Two-Sample KS test, comparing two sample series. Specifically, in the One-Sample KS test, the formula for the test statistic is:(9) D = max F x  i      − S ( x  i   )        where F x  i         represents the empirical distribution probability of the sample; S ( x  i   )    is the theoretical distribution probability of the sample.   3.4 Return period The concept of a "return period" relates to how often we can expect certain events to happen, like a specific intensity of rain or a flood. Think about it as the average wait time for nature's extreme events. It is a handy term used by those studying water and weather patterns to guess the likelihood of these big disasters coming about within a set period. In recent times, the renowned AND type and OR types have garnered considerable attention, corresponding to P ( X > x ∩ Y > y )    and P ( X > x ∪ Y > y )    respectively. The AND is the chance that both events X and Y go beyond certain levels at the same time, while the OR is the probability that either one exceeds a specific value. The “AND” type is employed in this study. Briefly, this type can be defined as:(10) AND type : T  u , v   = μ  1 − u − v + C ( u , v )       where μ   means the average arrival time of two consecutive events (in this study, μ = 1    since we study annual extreme events).  3.5 Calculation of flood coincidence probability 3.5.1 Coincidence of flood occurrence time The phenomenon of simultaneous flooding can be described as the condition in which the floodwaters of two rivers converge, demonstrating temporal overlap in half of the observed instances. This can be formally defined for a pair of rivers as follows:(11)  P  T   = P t  k   < T  i   < t  k + 1   , t  k   − τ  ij   < T  j   < t  k + 1   − τ  ij      = C t  k   , t  k   − τ  ij      + C t  k + 1   , t  k + 1   − τ  ij      − C t  k + 1   , t  k   − τ  ij      − C ( t  k   , t  k + 1   − τ  ij   )      In this study, within the Bantai, Wangjiaba, and Jiangjiaji gauges, the variables i   and j   denote two gauges and the flood occurs in gauge j   arrives at the confluence point later. The term T  i      refers to the specific day a flood event is observed at a given gauge. Lastly, τ  ij     is defined as the travel time gap of the last time of the floods travel from the gauges to the confluence point. Based on previous research and historical record, between the confluence of Bantai and Jiangjiaji gauges, the τ  ij     equals 1 day (Feng et al., 2018; Xue et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2021 ). When Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji gauges confluence, the τ  ij     euqals 0.  3.5.2 Coincidence of flood peak flow of Huai Basin The co-occurrence probability of overlapping flood magnitudes refers to the probability of both rivers simultaneously experiencing floods exceeding a certain value, and the expression for this probability is given as follows:(12) P Q  i   > q  i    T   ,  Q  j   > q  j    T      = 1 − u − v + C ( u , v )     Where Q  i     and Q  j     denote the magnitude of i   gauge and j   gauge; q  i    T     and q  j    T     represent the floods with the return period of T   years at i   gauge and j   gauge, respectively. The correlation of flood time and flood peak discharge is relatively small, and they can be regarded as independent events. Therefore, the occurrence of a flood event of a specified magnitude on a specified date during flood season can be represented as:(13) P  xy    T   = P  T   × P Q  i   > q  i    T   ,  Q  j   > q  j    T             3.6 Impacts of multivariate nonstationarity behaviors on flood coincidence probability The moving time windows are employed to obtain the time-varying parameters (Medina and Munoz., 2020; Wang et al., 2022 ). The window width should meet two basic requirements: firstly, the data within the given time window can be considered stationary, and secondly the data set of each time window is large enough to provide a good fit of the marginal distribution as well as the copula function. Then, the time window is shifted by one year each time step and the parameters of the marginal distributions and copula function can be estimated by MLE method. With the window sliding, the time series of each parameter are obtained. Then, we can combine different distribution parameters to analyze the effects on the coincidence probability of peak timing and peak flow. For example, in the timing coincidence between Bantai and Jiangjiaji, the parameters κ   and μ   of VM model, and the copula parameter θ   could create four combinations according to whether they are stationary (Figure S1 ): (1) κ   and θ   are nonstationary, and μ   is stationary. (2) μ   and θ   are nonstationary, and κ   is stationary. (3) All parameters are nonstationary. (4) κ   and μ   are stationary, and θ   is stationary. By controlling parameters, the impacts which the three parameters behavior on the coincidence probability of peaking time can be analyzed.   4 Results and analysis 4.1 Stationary coincidence probabilities 4.1.1 Establishment of marginal distributions and joint distributions Our primary aim was to ascertain the most likely point (MLP) (Figure S3 ) which has the highest probability of happening time of peak flood occurrences within the flood season of the Huai River, spanning from June 1st to September 30th. To achieve this, we applied the VM model to the complete flood occurrence time series data. Parameter estimation was conducted using the method of MLE, with the results detailed in  Table 1 . Specifically, the shape parameter κ for Bantai, Jiangjiaji, and Wangjiaba stations are 0.92, 1.12, and 1.11, respectively, while the location parameters μ are 2.44, 2.22, and 2.43, in the corresponding order. Furthermore, Table 1  includes results from the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test performed to assess the disparities between the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) and the theoretical sample distribution function. The findings indicate that, at a significance level of 5 %, the null hypothesis that there is no significant difference between the empirical and theoretical distributions cannot be dismissed. Effectively, the GEV distribution is harnessed for regional assessments of flood frequency as documented (Yan et al., 2021 ). Estimated via the maximum likelihood method, the most compelling parameter fittings are delineated in  Table 2 . To rigorously corroborate these fitted models, the KS test was the chosen instrument as a measure of fit quality. The KS statistic confirms that at a 5 % significance level, for all three stations, the GEV distribution is an effective choice to model their annual maximum flood peak discharges. With the marginal distributions established, the GEV model (depicted by the black curve) and empirical probabilities (marked with crosses) are presented in Figure S2 . The empirical data for Bantai and Wangjiaba closely align with the theoretical curve. At Jiangjiaji gauge, the observed divergence between the data points and the curve could be attributed to the limited length of the dataset. In our research, we employed a suite of copula models specifically, the bivariate symmetric Gaussian Copula, Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank Copulas to capture the interdependence between the hydrological events at Bantai and Jiangjiaji, as well as Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji. Our methodology hinged on a pseudolikelihood estimation that considers temporal rankings to accurately gauge the parameter θ. To discern the most fitting model for our data, we relied on the AIC and BIC for guidance. The performance of our selected copula was then scrutinized through the lens of the KS test. The outcomes of this rigorous assessment are laid out in  Table 3 . The findings, as the Table 3  reveals, spotlight the Frank Copula as the most adept at modeling the joint distributions for the time coincidence. Specifically, the estimated Frank Copula parameter θ for the concurrence of peak flood occurrences during the flood season between Jiangjiaji and Bantai is 2.46. For Jiangjiaji and Wangjiaba, the parameter is 4.61. Unlike the temporal analysis, the Gaussian Copula emerged as the copula with the lowest AIC and BIC values among the four functions tested in the peak flow coincidence events. Specifically, for the peak discharge coincidence of the Hong and Huai Rivers, the AIC and BIC values for the Gaussian Copula are −16.27 and −14.21, respectively. For the Shi River and Huai River, these values are even lower, at −38.1 and −36.04. The KS test values fall below the critical threshold, confirming the validity of the joint correlations estimated.  4.1.2 Stationary coincidence probability of flood peak timing or peak flow Accounting for the transforming time leads us to ascertain that a valid flood coincidence concurrence between Bantai and Jiangjiaji gauges occurs only if the flood at Bantai precedes that at Jiangjiaji by one day. For floods at Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji to occur concurrently on the same day, the flood coincidence incident may happen. Based on the joint distribution, we calculate the daily probability of flood encounters during the flood season. These probabilities are displayed in a frequency hygrogram, presented in Figure S3 . It is apparent from the data that the date of MLP between the Hong River and the Shi River is July 14th, respectively, with an encounter probability of approximately 3.41 × 10  − 4     . Likewise, the CP of MLP between the Huai River and the Shi River is 4.76 × 10  − 4     , which is expected around July 15th. Heatmap  Fig. 3  visualizes the exceedance CP of coinciding flood peak discharges at two stations for varying return periods. The image on the left depicts the joint probability of flood peak occurrence at Bantai and Jiangjiaji. It is clear that the probabilities for events with return periods of 1000 years, 100 years, 50 years, 20 years, 10 years, and 5 years are 6 × 10  − 5     , 1.4 × 10  − 3     , 3.6 × 10  − 3     ,1.28 × 10  − 2     , 3.37 × 10  − 2     , and 8.95 × 10  − 2     , respectively. On the other hand, the image on the right presents a heatmap showing the joint probability at Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji, where the respective probabilities for the same return periods are 1.7 × 10  − 4     , 2.76 × 10  − 3     , 6.47 × 10  − 3     , 2 × 10  − 2     , 4.76 × 10  − 2      and 0.114. Comparing the joint probabilities of Bantai-Jiangjiaji with those of Wangjiaba-Jiangjiaji reveals that the latter pairing exhibits higher probabilities, indicating a greater likelihood of simultaneous flood peak flow at Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji.   4.2 Time-varying coincidence probabilities induced by trend-caused nonstationary 4.2.1 Analysis of the impact of time parameters on the coincidence probability Before applying the moving time window analysis, we initially examined the overall trend of the time series. We observed a comparable probable trend across both datasets, as substantiated by the results of the Multivariate Mann-Kendall (MK) test. In both instances, the P values were notably less than 0.05, and the Z-values hovered around 2.2, collectively suggesting a consistent increasing trend across the groups which simply indicates that the peaking time of each gauge has postponed during flood season. Figure S4  graphically illustrate the dates of maximum floods during flood seasons over the years, with the solid lines tracing the chronological shifts in dates and the dashed lines depicting the overarching trend. Notably, the parallel nature of the dashed lines reveals a similar trend across the time series. Our study delved into the dynamics of dependence across varying time sequences by leveraging the time-dependent copula alongside a time-varying marginal distribution. Non-stationarity may manifest not only in the interdependence structure but also in the statistical characteristics of individual variables in a multivariate context (Bender et al.,2014 ).  Fig. 4  delineates how the VM distribution parameters κ and μ evolve over distinct 30-year intervals. When the condition is presumed to be stationary (ascertained by utilizing the entire series), the parameters are denoted by the grey line. For enhanced clarity on their evolution, we have drawn trend lines in red for each parameter. A closer inspection reveals that Bantai's κ parameter experiences the process of characterized by initial growth from 0.67 in the window 1959 to the window 1981, and then followed by a subsequent decline to 0.94 in the window 1986. However, the κ parameter of both Jiangjiaji and Wangjiaba exhibit a gradual downward trend over time. In contrast, the location parameter μ at each site evidences an annual increment. Significantly, the dotted lines of time-dependent VM parameters stray from their stationary counterparts during periods of pronounced change, underscoring a critical message: treating these time-sensitive parameters as stationary can lead to significant inaccuracies and compromise the reliability of further analysis. Employing a non-stationary copula framework, it becomes feasible to estimate the joint probabilities of the timing of flood events in every window. Given that the Frank copula exhibits the greatest fitting effect under stationary conditions, it has been adopted to interlink each marginal distribution in each window as well.  Fig. 5  illustrates how the temporal probabilities associated with the concurrence of peak flood events evolute. The Fig. 5  displays how the date and probability of MLP change when the parameters of the VM model vary respectively. When the location parameters μ   are stationary and κ   are time-dependent, just like Part a  and Part b  exhibit, the probability mostly fluctuated up and down. The CP of MLP of Hong River and Shi River first increased from 3.44 × 10  − 4      in 1959 to 4.2 × 10  − 4      in 1970 and then decreased to about 3.03 × 10  − 4      in 1985. Differ from this, the coincidence of Huai River and Shi River only has the tendency to decline from 5.94 × 10  − 4      to 3.47 × 10  − 4     . This difference can be attributed to the change of κ   of Bantai and Wangjiaba in Fig. 4  for the similarity trend between the CP and κ   of Bantai and Wangjiaba.  Compared to Part d  and Part h  whose parameters are both all nonstationary, it’s obvious that the location parameter κ   mostly affects the size of the highest probability. On the contrary, in Part b  and Part f  where location parameters μ   changes over time and κ   are valid, the transformation of the probability also changes regularly. The CP of MLP between Bantai and Jiangjiaji almost remains unchanged in Part b  but another circumstance has the tendency to grow in Part f . However, these changes are all smaller than the upper two pictures in term of the size of the highest probability. What we should pay more attention to are the variations of the happening time of MLP. Both pictures display the tendency to move backward in occurrence time of MLP from about July 10th to July 20th. Compared to the scale parameter κ  , the location parameters μ   are more vital in the aspect of the time and their increasing tendency has contributed to this postponement. The impact of θ   is primarily the values of the MLP, and the impact is weaker than the parameter κ   of VM model. Therefore, the marginal distributions have more effect on the coincidence compared to the copula function.  4.2.2 Analysis of the Impact of Parameters of GEV model on the the joint exceedance probability isolines Because the runoff of different rivers varies greatly, their trends also vary. For Wangjiaba station, the corresponding flows are 2674, 3052 and 3346 m³/s. For Jiangjiaji station, they are 2094, 3051 and 4170 m³/s and for Bantai station, they are 1335, 1711 and 2077 m³/s. The figures in the right top of each part are the coincidence probability of flood peak. Part a-c  is parallel to the three magnitudes equal to the 5-year,10-year and 20-year return period of Bantai and Jiangjiaji. As they clearly describe, the MLP of each year in them firstly increase and then drop down and the turning points are the window of 1980. The initial few CP of the MLP can be attributed to the flood peak flow for their small value, but the last few windows are obviously more effected by the peak timing for their same decline trend. Furthermore, we can observe that the MLP in the window of 1974 is higher than that in the window of 1973, with the rise percentage being 41 % and 56 % respectively for regression periods of 5 and 10 years. When the regression period reaches 20 years, the rise percentage goes up to 74 %. What’s more, the dashed line representing the stationary state is located below the nonstationary curves from the last twenty windows, indicating that the CP of the stationary state will underestimate the CP of the flood. Differ from Part a-c , Part d-f  which illustrate the CP between Jiangjiaji and Wangjiaba is more effected by the CP of flood peak flow. Especially for the 20-year return period, the CP of MLP suddenly dropped from the window of 1968 at 1.01 × 10  − 5      to 4.54 × 10  − 7     , with the decline ratio reaching as high as 95 %, which is negligible compared to the biggest MLP in all windows. This indicates that with time going on, the CP of MLP in great magnitude coincidence between Jiangjiaji gauge and Wangjiaba gauge at the same time has been out of the question. Obviously, the peak flow results in this change as their trends are similar just like the top right corner shows. Besides that, the dark dashed lines which are on behalf of the stationary state gradually rises above the set of non-stationary curves with magnitude largening. For example, in Part f , the CP of MLP equals 9.55 × 10  − 6      which is closed to the highest of all nonstationary curves at 1.02 × 10  − 5     . This transformation indicates that when calculating the CP of high magnitudes in these rivers, the stationary condition may overestimate the CP of great magnitudes.    5 Conclusions In this study, we leveraged the copula function to meticulously analyze the interconnected probabilities of the flood between Huai River and its tributaries, with a focus on assessing probability shifts in a dynamic, nonstationary environment. Our investigation was centered around two pivotal hydrological parameters: the timing of flood occurrences and the magnitude of peak discharges. Initially, our approach involved applying the VM model and GEV model to accurately characterize the marginal distributions for flood timing and peak flow rates. Subsequently, we employed sophisticated copula models to construct detailed joint distributions. This allowed us to compute the probabilities associated with various dates within the flood season and across a range of flood magnitudes. To gain deeper insights into temporal trends, we utilized the moving time window method. This technique was instrumental in elucidating how the probabilities of time and peak discharges fluctuated over time, especially when considering return periods of 20, 10, and 5 years in two distinct scenarios. The culmination of our research led to several key findings, which are succinctly summarized as follows: (1) Our findings indicate that the Huai River and its tributaries are most likely to experience coincidence floods in mid-July, with the CP of the MLP between the Wangjiaba and Jiangjiaji stations at 4.76 × 10  − 4     , which surpasses that between Bantai and Jiangjiaji. Therefore, it's crucial to reinforce flood defense efforts during this period. The convergence of the Huai River with the Shi River tends to be weaker both in terms of the timing and scale of floods when compared to the confluence of the Hong River with the Shi River. (2) With the help of moving time windows, we analyzed the transformation of the distribution variables and coincidence probability. The most likely happening coincidence date has the trend to move backward from July 10th to July 20th. The CP of MLP between the Bantai gauge and the Jiangjiaji gauge will become larger under nonstationary state when the time goes. But the probability between Shi River and Huai River has dropped down to a size after 1968 that can almost be disregarded, meaning the coincidence between them will be dominated by the minor floods. (3) The stationary results have lost its practicability in some coincidence phenomena. For example, the stationary curve has been above all the nonstationary lines in the Part f  of Fig. 8 , which confirms that the nonstationary research cannot be ignored. In our investigation of the flood coincidence between the Huai River and its tributaries, we employed copula functions in conjunction with an array of hydrological models tailored to fit marginal distributions. Our calculated probabilities lend a methodical basis to the decision-making processes in flood management. The non-stationary component of our research sheds light on potential shifts in flood trends. However, the span of available daily flow data imposes limits, obscuring potential long-term tendencies which might be teased out through increased copula compatibility. Besides that, the data we used is the daily average flow series which may lack precision than the daily maximum flow series. The data selection should be more scientific and rigorous in the future study. Future investigations will harness multidimensional hydrological models to delve into the complex interplay of flood timing across multiple rivers.
